propositions: A mutation removed a guard from a shell script allowing rm -rf /* to execute destructively on the host filesystem, destroying /opt/homebrew and homebrew-installed apps; only a subprocess timeout prevented /Users deletion.

execute_shard() spawns four subprocesses: baseline pytest and mutmut run execute test code (causal path for the incident); mutmut results and mutmut show do not, so only the first two require sandboxing.
Source-tree isolation (git archive) cannot prevent runtime filesystem effects from mutated code; OS-level sandboxing must deny writes outside an explicit allow-list.
macOS uses deprecated sandbox-exec with Seatbelt profiles; Linux requires bwrap; without either mechanism the run must abort non-zero; unshare fallback is rejected as unsafe.

Both test-executing subprocesses must run sandboxed with write-deny enforced on macOS (verified on-host) and Linux (CI verification pending); enforcement must be observed via filesystem checks, not argv inspection alone.
HOME must be set to a non-existent path in both sandboxed children; REBAR_MUTATION_ALLOW_UNSANDBOXED=1 waives the sandbox with a WARNING log but never silently falls back.
